newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai's Pudong grows at 20 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai's Pudong grows at 20 percent in 1996.

text.p: Shanghai's largest development zone, Pudong, grew significantly faster than Shanghai as a whole in 1996 with its gross domestic product (GDP) rising 20 percent year-on-year, Xinhua news agency reported on Monday.

The agency said the zone generated 52 billion yuan in GDP in 1996 with its growth rate eight percentage points higher than that of Shanghai as a whole, spurred by continuing large-scale investment in infrastructure.

The zone, to the east of Shanghai's city centre, added more than 800 foreign-funded enterprises in 1996, bringing the total to 4,265, with contracted overseas investment exceeding 12 billion U.S. dollars, Xinhua said.
Major infrastructure projects underway include construction of the Pudong international airport, the second-phase Waigaoqiao deep-water harbour and a subway line linking Pudong to Shanghai proper.
Pudong's development programme for 1997 is still being mapped out, the agency added.
